name: Korean Nachos

ingredients.name: nacho cheese sauce
ingredients.prep: made without hot sauce and kept hot

instructions.primary_message: Thinly slice the boneless ribeye. Peel, core, and finely dice the Asian pear. Finely dice the white onion. Mince the garlic. Cut the wonton wrappers in half diagonally. Drain the cabbage kimchi of excess liquid. Keep the made without hot sauce and of the nacho cheese sauce hot.
instructions.secondary_message:
1 ¼ lb boneless ribeye
1 Asian pear
½ medium white onion
4 medium cloves garlic
1 pkg wonton wrappers
1 ½ cups cabbage kimchi
1 recipe nacho cheese sauce

instructions.primary_message: In a large, sealable plastic bag, combine steak, pear, onion, garlic, ginger, soy sauce, brown sugar, vinegar, sesame oil, and black pepper. Seal and shake well to combine. Refrigerate for at least 1 hour and up to overnight.

Meanwhile, heat 1 inch of oil in a cast iron skillet to 350°F. Working in batches of 2 to 4 at a time, fry wonton wrapper halves until lightly golden, flipping once during frying; adjust heat to maintain oil temperature. Using a wire strainer or slotted spoon, transfer fried wontons to a paper towel–lined plate to drain. Sprinkle with salt while still hot. When oil has cooled, pour off all but 1 tablespoon.
Return skillet to medium heat and add kimchi. Cook, stirring occasionally, until softened and beginning to brown, about 10 minutes. Transfer kimchi to a plate and set aside.

Return skillet to high heat. Drain marinated beef and cook, stirring occasionally and working in batches if necessary to prevent crowding, until well browned, about 4 minutes; add oil, 1 tablespoon at a time, if skillet becomes too dry. Transfer beef to a plate, let skillet cool, and wipe out any excess oil.
Stir 2 tablespoons gochujang into cheese sauce and keep warm.

Preheat oven to 350°F (175°F). Using the cast iron skillet as a vessel, assemble the nachos in layers in the following order: wonton chips, beef, kimchi, cheese sauce, and shredded cheese, repeating as you go until the ingredients are used up. You may have some leftover wonton chips.
Bake until shredded cheese is melted and nachos are warmed through, about 5 minutes.

While nachos bake, mix together sour cream and lime juice. Drizzle baked nachos with lime sour cream and additional gochujang. Top with sesame seeds, cilantro leaves, scallion, and chile pepper slices, if desired. Serve immediately.

missing: wonton wrappers, cut in half diagonally

description: This Korean spin on nachos features bulgogi-style steak, caramelized kimchi, gochujang-spiked cheese sauce, and lime sour cream, all of it served on top of fried wonton chips.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 2 hr 5 min.

Optional or for serving: 1 fresh Asian red chile pepper, thinly sliced (optional)

Optional substitutions: boneless ribeye → sirloin steak; Asian pear → Bosc pear; Vegetable oil → canola oil; Kosher salt → sea salt

Notes: Gochujang is a Korean chili paste and can be found in Asian groceries and the international section of well-stocked supermarkets.
author: Morgan Eisenberg
